title: Me gusta, me encanta
summary: gustar and its flipped construction — me gusta / me gustan, me encanta

blocks.title: gustar flips the sentence
blocks.body: **gustar** doesn't work like 'to like' in English — it works backwards. It literally means 'to be pleasing to'. That's why we say *me gusta el café*: *el café* is the subject (the thing that pleases), and *me* is the person it pleases. The pronoun changes with the person; the verb changes with the thing.

blocks.title: gusta vs gustan — listen for the thing
blocks.body: If the thing you like is **singular** (or an infinitive), the verb is **gusta**: *me gusta el café*, *me gusta bailar*. If it's **plural**, the verb is **gustan**: *me gustan las tapas*. **encantar** ('to love', stronger than *gustar*) works exactly the same way: *me encanta el chocolate*, *me encantan los fines de semana*.
blocks.callout: The verb agrees with the thing liked, never with the person. There's no such thing as *yo gusto el café*.

pairs.note: The verb agrees with what's liked, not with *me*.

items.en: I don't like it at all

blocks.prompt: How do you say 'I love tapas' (a strong liking)?
blocks.explain: *las tapas* is plural, so the verb must be plural too: **encantan**. *Me encantan las tapas.*

blocks.hint: te + gusta (singular, el café) + the opening ¿.
blocks.explain: *¿Te gusta el café?* — *el café* is singular, so it takes *gusta*.

blocks.title: Construye con gustar
blocks.prompt: Combine a pronoun with a verb-and-thing phrase to build a sentence.

blocks.scene: Sofía asks about your tastes over tapas

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.en: Which tapas do you like most?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Me encanta la tortilla, y también me gustan las croquetas.
lines.en: I love tortilla, and I also like croquettes.

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.nl: Uy, no sé... a mí me gusta el pulpo, pero no me gusta nada el picante.
lines.en: Hmm, I don't know... I like octopus, but I don't like spicy food at all.

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.nl: Me gusta, pero prefiero una caña.
lines.en: I like it, but I prefer a beer.

questions.q: What does Sofía say she doesn't like at all?

blocks.prompt: Write 3 sentences about food or things you like, love, or don't like at all — use me gusta / me gustan / me encanta / no me gusta nada.
